func_1.title: What is a function?
func_1.explanation: Functions are like recipes! 📖 You write them once and can use them as many times as you want. Just "call" the function by its name and it does all the work!
options: A block of code we can reuse

func_2.title: return gives back a value
func_2.prompt: The return command is used to give back a result from the function.
func_2.explanation: return is like the function's postman! It takes the result and delivers it to whoever called the function. Without return, the function doesn't give back anything! 📬

func_3.title: Double a number
func_3.prompt: Create a function called "dobro" that takes a number and returns its double.
func_3.explanation: To double is to multiply by 2! So just return numero * 2. Simple as that! ✌️

func_4.title: Custom greeting
func_4.prompt: Create a function called "saudar" that takes a name and returns "Olá, <nome>!".
func_4.explanation: Use f-strings to build the text: f"Olá, {nome}!" or join texts with +: "Olá, " + nome + "!". Both ways work! 👋

func_5.title: Sum up to N
func_5.prompt: Create a function called "soma_ate" that sums all numbers from 1 to n.
func_5.explanation: Use a for loop from 1 to n and add them up! Start with soma = 0 and add each number. ➕

func_parsons_greet.title: Polite Greeting
func_parsons_greet.prompt: Assemble the function that says good morning to a person.
func_parsons_greet.explanation: We define the function first and then use it (call it) at the end.

func_6.title: Sum of Two Numbers
func_6.prompt: Complete the function to sum two numbers:
func_6.explanation: Functions can receive multiple pieces of information! Here a and b are parameters. To sum them, we use the plus sign (+). ➕

func_7.title: Reusing Functions
func_7.prompt: If I write `saudar()` 3 times in my code, what happens?
func_7.explanation: That's the magic of functions! You write the recipe once, and you can cook the dish as many times as you want by calling its name! 🍳🍳🍳

func_default_1.title: Default Values
func_default_1.explanation: Default parameters are like Plan B's! If no one provides a name, the function uses "Amigo". saudar() shows "Amigo", but saudar("Ana") shows "Ana"! 🎁
options: Throws an error because of = in parameter

func_default_2.title: Creating Default Value
func_default_2.prompt: Complete the function so that if no one passes the color, it uses "azul":
func_default_2.explanation: We put = after the parameter to give it a default value. cor="azul" means: if they don't say the color, use blue! 🎨

func_scope_1.title: Local Variables
func_scope_1.prompt: A variable created inside a function only exists inside it. True or false?
func_scope_1.explanation: Variables inside functions are "local" - they live only there! When the function ends, they disappear. It's like a secret that only the function knows! 🔒

turtle_house.title: Drawing a Circle
turtle_house.prompt: Let's create a function to draw a circle! Use the command turtle.circle(raio).
turtle_house.explanation: The command turtle.circle(50) draws a perfect circle with size 50! Functions make it easy to draw multiple identical shapes! 🔵

func_8.title: Secret Variable
func_8.prompt: Can I use a variable that I created INSIDE a function, OUTSIDE of it?
func_8.explanation: What happens in the function, stays in the function! Variables created inside are "local" and nobody outside can see them. It's a secret! 🤫
options: No, it's local and "dies" when the function ends
Yes, but only if you use the correct password

func_9.title: Rectangle Area
func_9.prompt: Complete the function that calculates the area (width times height):
func_9.explanation: Functions can receive multiple pieces of information! For the area, we need the width AND the height. We multiply both and we're done! 🟦

func_10.title: Ghost Parameter
func_10.prompt: Does a function's parameter exist outside of it? Ex: def func(nome): ... print(nome)
func_10.explanation: No! Parameters are like local variables. They only exist inside the function. Outside of it, Python doesn't know who they are! 👻

func_11.title: Return vs Print
func_11.prompt: What's the difference between `return` and `print` in a function?
func_11.explanation: `print` only shows on the screen (useful for humans). `return` gives the data to the program to use in other calculations! 📦
options: Return gives the value to the program, Print only shows on screen

func_12.title: Function Secret
func_12.prompt: If I create a variable inside a function, can I use it outside the function?
func_12.explanation: No! Variables created inside the function are "local". They are trapped in there and the rest of the program can't see them. It's like a secret diary! 🔒

func_13.title: Forgot the Argument
func_13.prompt: If `def oi(nome="Mundo"):`, what happens if I just call `oi()`?
func_13.explanation: Since we defined a default value ("Mundo"), Python uses it when we forget to pass the name! It's our Plan B! 🛡️

func_15.title: Many Defaults
func_15.prompt: Can a function have more than one parameter with a default value? Ex: `def func(a=1, b=2):`
func_15.explanation: Yes! You can have as many default parameters as you want, as long as they are at the end of the arguments list. It's like having multiple Plan B's! 🛡️

func_16.title: Full Date
func_16.prompt: Complete the function that takes day, month, and year:
func_16.explanation: Functions can take as much data as you want! Just separate them by commas. Day, Month, and Year make up the complete date team! 📅

boss_battle_6.title: The Master of Recipes
boss_battle_6.prompt: Create a function called "triplo" that takes a number and returns its triple. Then call triplo(4) and show the result.
boss_battle_6.explanation: The Master wants to see your recipe! Create the function and use it! 👨‍🍳
